title: The tzimtzum and the reshimu: the Essence hidden in the impression, in order to give
overview:
Chapter 12 explains the first *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu* it left, which the preface calls the main thing in the true unity: everything, even the whole chain of the *Kav*, is as nothing before Him, so that a person gives his will to the Essence alone and is not fooled by the *hishtalshelus*.

The analogies all say one thing. A teacher hides his depth and gives a child only a dot, yet the whole *pilpul* is in his mind and in the short law, as the Gemara is in the Mishna. The soul shrinks itself to live in the body, and its *tzelem* stays whole, as the phantom limb shows. The *reshimu* goes further: a blueprint, a sign, a thrown stone, a hint of the hand, a letter thrown across two hundred years, each more removed and each still carrying the self. Rabbi Markel adds an analogy of his own, the impression on a detective's notepad, and the seal in the wax, whose hollow is exact and backwards. And the point he presses most: the *tzimtzum* is not to withhold but *davka* to give, until the student is a Rebbe like his teacher. "A very big promise."

terms.gloss: contraction; here not a real one, since nothing is lost and it is done in order to give
the impression left after the tzimtzum: a withdrawal in which only a trace is left, and yet the whole self is in it
the giver, the teacher, who hides his depth in himself
the receiver, the student, for whose sake the contraction is made
an impression, a mark: the dot left of the teacher's depth, or the craftsman's sketch
Talmudic debate; the whole Gemara included in the short law of the Mishna
shortening; the Mishna, the little that holds the much, which is not yet a real tzimtzum
the form; more than an image: the whole form of the person, present from the first cell
a sign made as a reminder, like an acrostic or initials; unrelated to the thing itself
a hint, like a string around the finger or a movement of the hand, with nothing of the thing in it
a reversing seal: the hollow it leaves in wax has its exact shape, backwards
this opposite that; the reshimu as the inverted image of the original, the yetzer hara

sections.title: Preface: the tzimtzum and the reshimu are the heart of the true unity
sections.summary: The chapter turns to the first *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu* it left. Understanding them in depth is the main thing in the true unity: that everything, the whole chain of the *Kav*, is as nothing before Him, so that a person gives his will to the Essence alone and is not fooled by the *hishtalshelus*.

phrases.he: (יב) ומעתה יש להבין ביאור ענין הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
ובחינת הרשימו שנשאר כו'
הגם שידוע ליודעים,
phrases.en: even though in general people know about this,

phrases.he: הרי יש בזה פרטים רבים
וצריך להעמיק הדעת בהם ביותר
כי זהו עיקר היחוד האמיתי בעצמות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: the main thing in understanding in terms of the *yichud* is to understand the *inyan* of the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu*.

blocks.text: Now the *inyan* is the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*. In general people know about this, but there are many *pratim* (particulars) in it to go deep into, because the main thing in understanding the unity is to understand the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: איך דכולא קמיה כלא כו',
גם בבחינת כללות כל ההשתלשלות דקו וכו'
עד שיוכל אדם לכוון רצונו במסירת נפש לעצמות אור אין סוף לבדו
כמו שכתוב אתה הוא יהו״ה לבדך, אתה כו',

blocks.text: Everything before Him is as nothing, even the whole *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent) of the *Kav*, so that a person can give his will and his *mesirus nefesh* to the Essence of the *Ein Sof* alone and not get fooled by the whole *hishtalshelus*: "You are He, *Havaya*, alone."

phrases.he: וזהו המלך המרומם לבדו,
בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שלפני הצמצום
שמתנשא גם מימות עולם דאדם קדמון,
שנקרא ימי קדם הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: "The King who alone is exalted" is the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, raised even above the days of *Adam Kadmon*, called *yemei kedem*. Usually *yemos olam* is *Atzilus* and *yemei kedem* the *middos* of *Atik* and *Arich*; here it says a different thing.

phrases.he: וזהו השמים,
בחינת סובב הכללי שאחר הצמצום
ושמי השמים, שלפני הצמצום,
לא יכלכלוך,
גם בבחינת כלי לכלי,
phrases.en: a *kli* to a *kli*.

phrases.he: כמו גליף גליפו בטהירו עילאה כו'
phrases.en: even a *glif glifu* in the *tehiru ila'a* is not even a *kli* for a *kli* for the actual *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: ודי למבין
וכמו שכתוב מי לי בשמים,
שהוא גם בחינת סובב הכללי שלפני הצמצום שנקרא שמי השמים כו'
ועמך לא חפצתי בארץ,
בבחינת קו וחוט בחינת ממלא הכללי כו'

blocks.text: "The heavens" is the general *sovev* after the *tzimtzum*; "the heavens of the heavens", before it, "cannot contain You". *Yechalkelucha* means a *kli* to a *kli*: even the *glif glifu* in the *tehiru ila'a* is not a vessel for a vessel for the actual *Aibershter* (G-d).

"Whom do I have in heaven?": here "heaven" is what was called above "the heavens of the heavens", the general *sovev* before the *tzimtzum*; "on earth" is the *Kav* and thread, the general *memalei*. That is the preface; now comes the actual *inyan*.

sections.title: One pattern: the Essence hidden, so that the light can come with a leap
sections.summary: There are several analogies for the *tzimtzum*, but they all say one thing: for the light to flow as a *Kav*, the Essence of the light had to be hidden in itself, with only the merest edge left to shine, so that it can be drawn down by a leap across the gap.

phrases.he: והנה יש כמה אופנים במשלים שונים
להשכיל ביאור ענין הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי כידוע למעיין
וכללותו עולה בסגנון א',
phrases.en: But in general it's one *inyan*.

phrases.he: והוא כדי שיוכל להיות אור אין סוף בבחינת השפעה בצמצום בבחינת קו,
הוצרך לצמצם עצמות אורו שישאר בהעלם בעצמותו כו'
ולא יאיר כולו, רק אפס קצהו בלבד
כדי שיהיה אחר כך המשכות האור בדילוג הערך

blocks.text: There are several *meshalim* for the *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui*, but in general it is one *inyan*: for there to be a flow in a contracted way, as a *Kav*, He had to contract the Essence of His light so that it stays hidden in His Essence.
Not all of it shines, only the merest edge, so that afterwards the light can be drawn down *b'dilug ha'erech*, by a leap. That is the *inyan* of the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu*; now come the *meshalim*.

sections.title: The first analogy: the teacher's Mishna holds the whole Gemara
sections.summary: A teacher hides his depth in himself and gives a small student only a dot. But it is not a real *tzimtzum*: the whole *pilpul* is in his mind and in the short law, as the Gemara is in the Mishna, and the whole point of the contraction is to give, until the student becomes a Rebbe like him.

phrases.he: והרי זה כמשל אור שכל עמוק ורחב שבעצמות המשפיע
שכדי שיומשך ממנו למקבל הבלתי ערך אליו,
הוצרך המשפיע להעלים בעצמו כל עומק השגתו,
ולא ישאר רק בחינת רושם, כנקודה א',
מכל העומק והרוחב

blocks.text: The first *mashal*: the deep and broad intellect of the *mashpia* himself. For it to reach a *mekabel* not on his level at all, the giver has to hide in himself the whole depth of his comprehension, leaving only a *roshem*, like one dot, of all the depth and breadth.

phrases.he: ולא שנסתלק ונתעלם לגמרי
phrases.en: It's not that it actually disappears,

phrases.he: רק כמו השונה בדרך קצרה,
phrases.en: it's like a Mishna in relationship to the Talmud,

phrases.he: שכל העומק ורוחב הפלפול ישנו בשכלו,
phrases.en: that when he says a Mishna, he knows the whole Gemara on it,

phrases.he: רק שהוא נכלל לפי שעה בהעלם עצמותו
בשעה שאומר הדין דרך קיצור
phrases.en: when he's saying the Mishna in a short way.

phrases.he: ומיד שישאלוהו ירחיב הדבר כו'
phrases.en: The minute somebody will ask him, he'll be able to tell you the whole big *pilpul* on it.

phrases.he: רק בשביל שיובן למקבל דרך זה הקצר, מעלים גם בעצמו לפי שעה כו'
phrases.en: Because he is teaching little children *Mishnayos*, so even inside of himself he is hiding it for the time being,

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות
phrases.en: like it explains in another place at length.

blocks.text: It does not actually disappear, because this all happens in the *mashpia* himself. It is like a Mishna to the Talmud: when he says a Mishna he knows the whole Gemara on it, only included in him, hidden, while he says it the short way. "The minute somebody will ask him, he'll be able to tell you the whole big *pilpul* on it."
So that the receiver will understand by this short way, he hides it for the time being even in himself, because he is teaching little children Mishnayos, as it explains elsewhere at length.

phrases.he: 13 ומה שנשאר כמו נקודה, שהוא דרך קצרה,
phrases.en: And what is left like a *nekuda*, which is a short way,

phrases.he: אין זה צמצום גמור ואמיתי
phrases.en: first of all, it's not a total *tzimtzum*, and secondly, it's not even a real *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: כמו המצמצם ומעלים לגמרי,
phrases.en: like somebody who actually makes a real *tzimtzum* and totally hides it,

phrases.he: שנחסר למקבל לגמרי
phrases.en: that over there it's missing by the *mekabel* totally.

blocks.text: What is left like a dot, the short way, is not a total and real *tzimtzum*: first, it is not total, and second, not even real. It is not like one who contracts and hides altogether, so that by the *mekabel* it is totally missing.

And it is not only not that: it is *mamash* the opposite. The whole reason it is done is *davka davka* to give it over to the *mekabel*. A *tzimtzum* means something is going away; this *tzimtzum* is in order to give, not to stop it.

blocks.title: One fishy plus one fishy
blocks.text: A teacher teaching little kids mathematics has to *metzamtzem* (contract) the whole thing, and more, *megashem* it, make it physical: one fishy plus one fishy; if you have an apple and another apple; if you have four apples and you eat an apple... In the beginning he can tell them only tiny little things, not to withhold the information but just the opposite: he wants to give them all of it, so that from first grade they get to second, all the way up to post-graduate work, and finally become a Rebbe just like him.

The goal is not that they will know as much as he does; the goal is that they will be a Rebbe just like him. The actual *Atzmus* (essence) is given over: when they finish, it is not a guy who knows a bunch of knowledge, but one who *mamash* has the *etzem* of a Rebbe himself.

phrases.he: אלא הענין הוא שכולל בדרך קצר זה כל האריכות,
לא יחסר דבר וחצי דבר

blocks.text: The short way includes all the length; not a thing, not half a thing, is missing. So it is not like a summary in a *goyishe* (non-Jewish) school: the *mashal* has to be *davka* a Jewish one, the Mishna, because the Mishna is not a *kitzur* (shortening) that leaves things out. Nothing is missing; the whole Talmud is included in it.

sensitivity.reason: Contrasts a "goyishe" school, whose summaries leave things out, with a Jewish one.
sensitivity.publishable: The short way includes all the length; not a thing, not half a thing, is missing. So it is not like an ordinary summary in school: the *mashal* has to be the Mishna, because the Mishna is not a *kitzur* (shortening) that leaves things out. Nothing is missing; the whole Talmud is included in it.

phrases.he: כמו שכלול בדין הקצר שבמשנה
כל האריכות הפלפול שבגמרא

blocks.title: Rebbi, the Romans, and the Gemara before the Mishna
blocks.text: Not only does the Mishna hold the *pilpul* because he knows it; just the opposite: the *pilpul* of the Gemara came out of the Mishna. Rebbi saw that the Romans were making problems and the yeshivos were getting messed up. People think first came the Mishna and then the Gemara, "but really there was a Gemara before the Mishna." They had the whole *Torah sheb'al peh* (Oral Torah), and he put it in a very short way so that it could be *shone*, gone over fast, and said it so that later, when things were forgotten, they could reconstitute them out of the Mishna. The whole previous Gemara is included in the *kitzur* of the Mishna, and the whole *pilpul* comes back out of it.

phrases.he: וכמו שלא נעלם ליודע כל הפלפול
גם בשעה ששונה לעצמו דרך קיצור כו'
שנמצא שידיעתו באריכות מקפת בהעלם כל התגלות הקיצור
ולא שנסתלק לגמרי כשכחה
phrases.en: It's not that it really went away, like he forgot it.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא כו'
וכמו שכתוב ביאור זה באריכות במקום אחר.

blocks.text: When somebody really knows the whole Gemara, a big *talmid chacham* like they had in the olden days, even when he says a Mishna he knows the whole thing, as if Rashi were saying a Mishna. His knowledge at length encompasses, hidden, everything revealed in the short version.
It did not go away, as in forgetting, like somebody with amnesia, *chas v'shalom* (Heaven forbid). He knows the whole thing right now, even while he says it the short way.

sections.title: The second analogy: the soul's life in the body, the phantom limb and the tzelem
sections.summary: The soul has to hide and shrink itself to become the life of the flesh, yet the physical life stays bound to it: joy and pain are felt in the soul, and when the soul leaves there is no life. A lost limb is not lost to the soul, as the phantom limb shows, because the soul's *tzelem*, the whole form, hovers over the body and is there from the first cell.

phrases.he: ואופן משל הב' מחיות הנפש בגוף
גם כן עולה על דרך הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: It also comes in the same way.

phrases.he: והוא בהיות שכדי שישתנה מחיי רוחניים שבעצם הנפש לחיי בשר,
הוצרך להיות בחינת העלם וכיווץ האור של הנפש בתחלה
לפי שאין ערך ביניהם
phrases.en: it's a totally different *inyan*.

blocks.text: The second analogy, the life of the soul in the body, comes out the same way. For the spiritual life of the soul to become the life of the flesh, the light of the soul first has to hide and shrink, because there is no comparison between them. The soul as it is cannot come into the body.

Not even one power of the soul can, as with Abbott and Costello and the Wolf Man: if the whole *koach hatnua* (power of motion), or the *koach hadibur* (power of speech), tries to come in, there will be no motion at all. Certainly the whole soul cannot: it is too infinite for the body, and there is no comparison: **it's a totally different *inyan***.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה הרי מתפעלת הנפש ממקרי הגוף
phrases.en: But nonetheless, the soul is *mispa'el*, it gets excited from what happens to the body.

phrases.he: אם כן גם אור הגשמת החיות
phrases.en: the light of the *hagshamas hachayus*, which is the actual physical life,

phrases.he: תתחבר ונקשר אל אור עצמותה הרוחני
phrases.en: So it's connected.

phrases.he: כצמיחה גשמית
שנקשר בכח הצומח הרוחני כו'
phrases.en: that it's connected to the *koach hatzomeach haruchani*.

blocks.text: And still the soul is *mispa'el* (moved) by what happens to the body, bad or good. If so, the light of the life made physical, the actual physical life, is joined and bound to the spiritual light. **So it's connected.**

As the Mishna is completely connected to the Gemara, the physical life is completely connected to the spiritual, and you see it two ways. The actual happiness and sadness are in the soul, not the body. And "dead dogs don't bark": the minute the soul leaves, there is no life of the flesh at all. The spiritual life is *makif* (encompassing) on the physical.

blocks.title: The plant out of the ground
blocks.text: Like physical growth, which is bound to the spiritual power of growth: you see that if you take the plant out of the ground, it stops growing.

phrases.he: ובהחתך אבר הגוף
phrases.en: And another proof of this is that if somebody accidentally loses a limb, like an arm or a leg or something like that, *chas veshalom*,

phrases.he: לא יחסר באור וחיות רוחניות של אבר זה
phrases.en: the spirituality of it will not be missing anything.

phrases.he: וראיה מסומא שמוליד שלם כו' כידוע
phrases.en: that somebody who, *chas veshalom*, gets blind, it doesn't mean that from now on all his children will be like that, but rather they are born whole.

blocks.text: Another proof: if somebody accidentally loses a limb, an arm or a leg, *chas v'shalom*, nothing is missing from the spiritual light and life of that limb. Its spirituality is not missing anything.

The proof from a blind man: one who, *chas v'shalom*, becomes blind does not have blind children; they are born whole. The same with any limb: a man who loses a finger does not have generations missing that finger. "Just the opposite, they will actually have a finger."

blocks.title: The phantom limb
blocks.text: People who lose a piece of their body still feel it there, like a ghost: it is called the phantom limb. Some even have a problem: "it itches and you can't itch it."

phrases.he: אין זה רק שהרוחניות הוא בהעלם,
וישנו במציאותו,
חופף על חיות הגשמי שבגוף
ונקרא צלם איש כו'
phrases.en: And that's called a phantom person. It's not really a phantom person, it's the *tzelem*.

phrases.he: והיינו על דרך הנזכר לעיל בידיעה שבהעלם כו'
(וכל זה מבואר באריכות במקום אחר)

blocks.text: The spirituality is only hidden: it is there, hovering over the physical life of the body, and it is called the *tzelem* of a man. A phantom person, only not really: the *tzelem*. In English it is a picture, an image, but more than an image: the form. *B'tzalmeinu kidmuseinu* is "in our image", but in Hebrew *tzelem* means that the whole actual form of the person is there.

This *tzelem*, by a tree and by a person, is already in the first cell. When he is conceived, with only one or two cells, if you knew how to look you would see exactly how he will look grown up. The whole code is already there: frog or person, dog or horse, *mamash* the color of his eyes and how smart he will be, not by education but in potential, even to the tiniest detail. You could even get his fingerprints.

blocks.title: The family with the heart attacks
blocks.text: Someone in the class had heard it on the news that day: a study of a family of about a hundred people with a very strong propensity for heart attacks. Of about ten siblings nine have heart trouble, and their offspring too. They studied the genetic codes and found one tiny protein missing; that is the reason. The one brother without the missing protein has no heart attacks, and of the offspring, those missing it have heart trouble or will have it; the others do not. One tiny protein out of the whole genome, and you could see it in the first cell: by the first cell it is already there.

From the minute of conception, when the male and female parts join, it is there; really even before that, in two pieces; and before those, in the genetic makeup of his father and his mother, only you do not know which pieces he will get from each. The spirituality, the form, the *tzelem*, is there before that. All this is explained at length elsewhere.

sections.title: More of the same: the power of motion, and being smart
sections.summary: The spiritual power of motion has to contract itself to come into physical motion, or there is no motion at all, as with a man who freezes in fright; and the same holds for many other things, like the smartness of a particular intellect.

phrases.he: וכן כח התנועה הרוחניות כשבאה בתנועת הגשם,
מתצמצמת בעצמותה כו'
ועם כל זה התנועה גשמית מחוברת ומקושרת בתנועה הרוחנית
וכהאי גוונא באופנים אחרים
phrases.en: this is exactly the same *mashal* you can say in many different ways,

phrases.he: כמו ענין התחכמות שכל פרטי מכח המשכיל שלו ששורה עליו בהעלם כו'.

blocks.title: The dinosaur in the street
blocks.text: So too the spiritual power of motion contracts itself in its essence to come into physical motion. A guy is walking down the street and all of a sudden a dinosaur comes up. With no *tzimtzum* of the spiritual motion into the physical, there is no physical motion: "He'll freeze." He cannot make any motion at all.

blocks.title: Calm down and you'll be able to tell me
blocks.text: Or a guy is very excited: he just saw the Twin Towers fall, and the cop is telling him, "Calm down for a minute, and you'll be able to tell me." The cop is trying to make a *tzimtzum*, so that he can get the speech out of the *koach hadibur*.
The same *mashal* can be said in many different ways: *hischakmus* (being smart) in a particular intellect, from the power of his mind, which was in him hidden, and all kinds of other things.

sections.title: The reshimu: the blueprint and the sign
sections.summary: The *reshimu* means a withdrawal, with only an impression left. The analogies go down by steps, which a later discourse matches to the four worlds: the Mishna is the same thing as the Gemara; a blueprint is a different thing with the whole shape in it; a sign, like lecture notes or an acrostic, only reminds, and is unrelated to the thing itself.

phrases.he: ואמנם להבין בחינת הרשימו
שענינו מורה בחינת הסתלקות בהעלם
ולא נשאר מהכל רק רושם כו'

blocks.text: But the *reshimu* means a withdrawal into hiding, with nothing left but an impression. The first analogies were not really that: the Mishna, though a *kitzur*, is the same *inyan* as the Gemara, *hamu'at hamachzik es hamerubeh*, the little that holds the much. Nothing there is totally gone.

blocks.title: Four analogies in a later discourse
blocks.text: By the way, he was reading in a discourse, of 5679 he thinks (he would have to look at the book again), that there are basically four *inyanim* here, though you see more than four *meshalim*: the Mishna and the Gemara; the *reshimas oman*, the craftsman's blueprint; the *os*, like an acrostic; and last a *remez* (a hint). The soul's life in the body is also a small thing that holds a big thing: the motion is a different *inyan*, yet still the motion that was included in the original motion; it is not a total removal, something is left over. And the throwing, he says, is the actual *inyan* of the *reshimu*, a separate thing.

blocks.title: The analogies and the four worlds
blocks.text: He says the four are like the four worlds. *Atzilus* is like a *kitzur*: still the same *inyan* as the *Atzmus*, though a big *kitzur* of it. The *remez*, a totally different *inyan*, is like *Asiya*. Between them he names *Beriya* as the *roshem* and *Yetzira* as "like a map of a big thing", where the *tzura* (form) is still there, and speaks of the *tziyunim* (markers), like *rashei teivos* (initials), where the thing is *mamash* gone but the first letter is left; which goes with *Beriya* and which with *Yetzira* is not clear on the tape.
It is an interesting thing: when you read the Rebbe Rashab, he fills in stuff from here. But you have to know it over here first, before you read it over there.

Here we do not necessarily have to know how it applies in the four worlds. What you see is that there are different *meshalim*, and one, the Mishna and the Gemara, shows how the whole thing is *mamash* there, with nothing at all missing: the whole Gemara is right there in the Mishna.

phrases.he: הוא מובן יותר מענינים משלים אחרים,
כמו הרושם שעושה האומן
שיוכל לעשות הבנין בקיצור קו זה שברושם,
שכולל כל אריכות המעשה בקיצור רושם זה

blocks.text: It is understood better from other analogies, like the *roshem* (impression) a craftsman makes, that is, a blueprint. In this little sketch is the whole *inyan* of exactly how to build a building, all the length of the work in its brevity.

phrases.he: או כמו שעושה לזכרון הנקרא אות
phrases.en: just like an *os*, like a sign.

phrases.he: שאין האות ענין שייך אל עצם הענין,
רק לזכרון בעלמא,
phrases.en: just in order to remember.

phrases.he: כמו עשה לך ציונים כו'

blocks.question: Why is the blueprint not as good a *mashal* as the teacher and the student?
blocks.text: Because it is a different *inyan*. The Mishna is the same *inyan* as the Gemara: *chachma* and *chachma*. The blueprint is not a building, only the shape of one. From the Mishna, where not even half a thing is missing, you can reconstitute the whole Gemara; from the blueprint too, but not exactly, because it is a different *inyan*: "This is a building and this is a drawing."

blocks.question: Is the Mishna the analogy for the *tzimtzum*, showing that the whole thing is included in it, and the blueprint and the others are analogies for the *reshimu*?
blocks.text: No. Later on the text speaks of the *reshimu*: the throwing is the analogy for the *reshimu* itself. And the Mishna is also like a *reshimu*: there is a *tzimtzum*, he is *metzamtzem* and leaves over a *roshem*. It is a *reshimu*, and it is called *reshima*.

blocks.title: The notes from the lecture
blocks.text: You know the *Reshimos* of the Rebbe? A *reshima* is the notes a guy takes sitting in a lecture in school. In his little notes is the entire lecture. "Where's the whole lecture? I don't see the whole lecture." But he wrote it for himself, in a short way he understands, so when he looks at it he remembers the whole lecture. That is the next *inyan* here.
That is like what one makes as a reminder, called an *os*: not just notes, even less than notes, only a sign. The sign has nothing to do with the thing itself.

blocks.title: Every Good Boy Does...
blocks.text: Like tying a string around your finger, though that is really a *remez*. An *os* is like *tziyunim*, like *rashei teivos*; or in the passage read on Pesach, what's-his-name made *tziyunim*: *Detzach Adash B'achav*, more than *rashei teivos*, made into a thing of its own. Or "Every Good Boy Does...", whatever it stands for: a little nonsense verse. There are various such things, made as *tziyunim* to remember by.

phrases.he: וזהו בחינת העלם יותר מקיצור ההלכה ששונה וכולל בו הכל
שעל כל פנים שייך ענין הקיצור אל האריכות

blocks.text: This is more hidden than the short law, where at least the short belongs to the long. If you find money there is a whole *pilpul*, but the *inyan* is finding money: in the Mishna that is *mamash* the *inyan* you are talking about. The *os* is not the *inyan* at all, only a reminder.

He doesn't know what the acrostic stands for; green something, he thinks. That is the *inyan*: if you do not know what it is for, you cannot figure it out. Not like the Mishna: even if you cannot figure out the whole *pilpul* of the Gemara, you know they are talking about a guy who hit another guy, or a donkey that stepped on something; even the short version has the *halacha*, you just do not know how they derived it. It says explicitly: a donkey. Here you do not know what they are talking about: "every good boy" is not really about good boys.

sections.title: Hidden still more: the thrown stone, the hand's hint, the written word
sections.summary: The real analogy of the *reshimu* is the thrown stone: far from the thrower, yet his whole power of motion, and he himself, is in it, so anyone whose window it broke can sue him. Further away still is a hint with the hand, which has nothing to do with the idea, and the writing that carries a teacher's mind across two hundred years.

phrases.he: ויש עוד אופן ברשימו זו
שהוא מורה ענין הצמצום וההעלם הרבה יותר

blocks.text: And there is another kind of this *reshimu*, which shows the *tzimtzum* and the hiding much more, and this already shows the actual *inyan* of the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: והוא כמו הזורק אבן,
שכח המוליך אותו נבדל מן העצם
ועם כל זה
phrases.en: but nonetheless,

phrases.he: כל כח התנועה מלובש בו בהעלם
אך שהוא בריחוק נבדל ביותר מכחו העצמי שבידו
מה שאין כן כח התנועה עצמה שמניעה בעצמו בגשם
שמלובש בגלוי בגשם ביותר כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: One who throws a stone, where the power that carries it is separate from the self. You see a ball rolling down the street and you know somebody kicked it, but you cannot even see the person anymore.

blocks.title: You broke the window
blocks.text: And still the whole power of motion is dressed in it, hidden. If the stone comes through your window you can sue the thrower, because his power of motion is dressed in the stone; not only the power of motion, but the actual intention of the self. He says the stone broke your window, and he was nowhere near it. "Doesn't matter, you broke the window." Or the song *I Shot the Sheriff*: what do you mean I shot him? The bullet got the sheriff. So the actual *etzem* is dressed in it.

Only it is far away, very separate from his own power in his hand, unlike moving something he holds, which is connected to it. Elsewhere in *Chassidus* this *mashal* is given for *Malchus*, holding the thing in his hand, and *Malchus* of *Malchus*, throwing it away.

phrases.he: ויש בחינת העלם יותר גם מזה,
phrases.en: There's an even bigger *helem*,

phrases.he: שדומה לענין הרושם לזכרון לבד
phrases.en: like a *roshem* just for a remembrance.

blocks.text: A hiding greater still: the impression only as a reminder. Not like an acrostic: *rashei teivos* are still the letters, telling you words that begin with them. This is a string around your finger, only a *remez*. The string doesn't tell you it must have something to do with strings; it has nothing at all to do with string.

phrases.he: והוא כמו הרומז בידו לאיזה שכל עמוק ביותר
phrases.en: that a very heavy *sechel* can be enclothed.

phrases.he: שנבדל תנועה גשמית מהשכל הרוחני,
ועם כל זה מבין השכל מתוכו כו'

blocks.text: One who hints with his hand at some very deep idea: a very heavy *sechel* can be dressed in it. The physical motion is separate from the spiritual idea, and nonetheless one understands the idea from it.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's hand at the farbrengen
blocks.text: At a *farbrengen* the Rebbe would make a *chizuk* with his hands, and everybody would freak out. What are they freaking out for? He isn't telling them anything; he's moving his hand. But they see what the Rebbe is telling them: "Oh, be strong!"

Or the V-sign; though that is really a letter: V for victory. "That's the funny thing": by the hippies it became peace. "It doesn't mean peace. It means exactly the opposite of peace": winning the war, *netzach*. So it is not a *remez* but a *tziyun*, *rashei teivos*.

sensitivity.reason: A jab at the hippies for turning the victory sign into a peace sign.
sensitivity.publishable: Or the V-sign; though that is really a letter: V for victory. It means winning the war, *netzach*. So it is not a *remez* but a *tziyun*, *rashei teivos*.

blocks.text: Or you blink your eye to tell a guy something, and all kinds of movements: the movement has nothing to do with the concept, and yet he understands the concept from it.

phrases.he: ויותר מזה העלם אור השכל בתנועת האצבע בכתיבתו אותו
phrases.en: And even more than that is the light of the *sechel* which is enclothed in the movement of the finger when it writes it,

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות

blocks.text: More hidden still is the light of the intellect in the movement of the finger as it writes: it is writing down the *sechel*, and yet it is just a motion.

blocks.title: A stone thrown across two hundred years
blocks.text: Farther away still is a combination of the two: a letter. While your hand is moving and writing, it is connected: that is *Malchus*. But then you can take it like a stone and throw it over two hundred years, which is what we have in front of us: the Rebbe wrote this down and threw it, not only through space but through time, and it came to us. The letters have nothing in them: ink on paper, copied from other ink on paper, copied from the manuscript, then photographed, a *reshimu* of a *reshimu* of a *reshimu*, "and yet the whole *sechel* is enclothed in it."

sections.title: It all says one thing: a contraction in order to give, and the seal in the wax
sections.summary: Every analogy says that the Essence itself stays, hidden, in the impression, and that the contraction is not one: it is *davka* to give the receiver everything, until the student is a Rebbe like his teacher. Each analogy has what the others lack, and the *reshimu* is like the hollow a seal leaves in wax: exact, and backwards.

phrases.he: והכל עולה לסגנון א' הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: All of these things is really telling you only one thing:

phrases.he: שבחינת העצמות נשאר בהעלם וכלול ברושם ונקודה זו כו'
ודי למבין:

blocks.text: It all comes to one pattern: the Essence stays hidden and is included in this impression. Not just the intellect of it but the *etzem*, the actual selfness, and that is why you say he broke the window.

Back to the teacher. His *tzimtzum* is certainly not to hide, and not even to give over the little part he gives over, or even his intellect; just the opposite, it is to give over the *etzem*, so that the *talmid* (student) grows up to be a Rebbe too.

That is the one pattern: the *tzimtzum* is not a *tzimtzum*, and it is not in order to contract; just the opposite. By the *mashpia* it is surely not one: when the teacher says the Mishna he knows the whole Talmud. But even by the *mekabel* it is not a *tzimtzum*: its whole reason is *davka* to give over the whole *Atzmus* to him.

And the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for): the *Aibershter* is going to give it all over to us, to the Jew, so that the student is a Rebbe; He is going to grow us up to be just like Him. That is the promise in the *tzimtzum*, and it is a very big promise.

blocks.question: Why does he use all these analogies, each one less than the one before?
blocks.text: One reason is what he told them: they represent the *tzimtzumim* in the different worlds. But then why are the worlds contracted that way, each one less than the world before?

And why is each *mashal* less than the one before? As they were saying the other day from *Pasach Eliyahu*, the worlds are themselves *meshalim*, to learn about the *Aibershter*. The *hishtalshelus* we are learning, how the world is constructed, is a *mashal* all the way down to us.

blocks.question: So each analogy gives a different aspect of the *reshimu*, one the others do not, and taken together they give a fuller picture?
blocks.text: Yes: *lo re'i zeh k're'i zeh*, each has what the other does not. No *mashal* should be taken by itself; in the *nimshal* it is truly the whole thing. The Mishna and the Gemara give you that the whole thing is there, not a thing, not half a thing missing: that is very clear in the first *mashal*.

The problem with the first *mashal*: it is not really a total *tzimtzum*. Nothing is missing, but it is a *kitzur*, a *mu'at hamachzik*, a small thing that holds a big thing, not a nothing. *Tzimtzum* means it was totally gone and only a *reshimu* is left, a *reshimu b'alma*, a mere impression: the original thing is gone.

blocks.title: The impression on the detective's notepad
blocks.text: This one is not in the book; Rabbi Markel made it up. In the detective books they come in and find a notepad: the page with the telephone number or address is gone, but the page under it has an impression, and in the impression is the actual number. The whole thing is there.

blocks.title: The seal in the wax
blocks.text: A *reshimu* is also a *chosam hamis'hapech* (a reversing seal). You stick the seal into the wax and take it out. The seal is gone and an empty space is left, but in the empty space is the exact shape of the seal, only backwards: inverted, *zeh l'umas zeh* (this opposite that).

So the *reshimu* is *mamash* the *yetzer hara* (the evil inclination): the bad, the *l'umas zeh*, is the *reshimu*. It is what was left in the *chalal* (the space), backwards: where the original is in, the *reshimu* is out, and where it is out, the *reshimu* is in. Everything is backwards, and reversed too.

blocks.title: A mold of a mold
blocks.text: Like making a face: they put plaster, or a mold, on the guy's face and take it off. There is a face, exactly the opposite: where it went out it goes in, where it goes in it goes out. So you take a mold of the mold, and it comes out straight.

By going away from evil, you go towards the good: by reversing the *l'umas zeh* you go towards the *Aibershter*, because it is *mamash zeh l'umas zeh*. Where the original says good, the *l'umas zeh* says bad: "Oh, I don't want to get married. I want to just hang out." The original is the exact opposite.

That is *mamash* the *reshimu*, the *chosam hamis'hapech*: an empty space is left, and in it an exact *reshimu*, backwards from the original. Leave the face cast, and the empty space is the exact shape of the face, backwards. Not really backwards, though: the space is the exact shape, and only the borders are backwards. In the seal too the space is the same shape, and it is the *kli* that is backwards. That too is what a *reshimu* means: an impression.

Back to the *meshalim*. The first has it that it is all there. The second gives a better idea: it is not really a house, yet you can reconstruct the whole house from it; but it is still too much: not the same *inyan*, yet the whole shape is exactly the original. The third you *mamash* cannot reconstruct unless you are the original guy. The fourth gives the best idea that it is totally *nivdal* (separate); yet in the final *remez* too the whole thing is really there, only not so clear as in the Mishna and Gemara. And that is the reason why.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is the teacher's dot "not a total and real *tzimtzum*", and what is the goal of the contraction?
In what sense was the Gemara before the Mishna, and what does that show about the short way?
What do the phantom limb and the first cell show about the *tzelem*?
Why is an *os* more hidden than the short law of the Mishna?
How does suing the thrower for the stone through the window show that the self is dressed in the thrown stone?
What does the seal in the wax add to the meaning of *reshimu*, and what is backwards in it?

He stops to take a phone call.

notes.text: Class 007 line 8: he says that usually yemos olam is Atzilus and yemei kedem the middos of Atik and Arich, "like I said before"; kept as he said it.
Line 23 begins with "13" in the chapter text (apparently a page or paragraph mark); rendered "[13]".
Line 42 is not read in class (the alignment marks no reading); its phrase is a plain rendering.

The discourse he was reading: he hesitates between several years ("I think it was" 5679, "I have to look at the book again"); later he speaks of the Rebbe Rashab filling in from here. The block says "of the year 5679 he thinks". Its matching of analogies to worlds is garbled in the transcript after Beriya (he names Beriya as the roshem, then speaks of Yetzira and "a map", then of the tziyunim, then the remez as Asiya); the block gives his clear claims (Atzilus the kitzur, the remez Asiya), reports the Beriya and Yetzira words as he says them, and says the matching is unclear on the tape.

"What's his name made tziyunim": the simanim of the plagues in the Haggada are Rabbi Yehuda's; he does not name him and the block does not either. "Every Good Boy Does Fine" is the lines of the treble staff, not the rainbow; he could not remember and the block leaves it so.
The story of Rebbi and the Romans: he misspeaks ("first was the Gemara and then there was the Talmud"); the block gives what he means, that people think the Mishna came first and the Gemara after.
He says one could read even the fingerprints from the first cell; fingerprints are not fully set by the genes. Left as he said it.
The question "why does he use all these meshalim, each progressively lesser" comes after he asks to turn off the tape; taken as a student's, since he answers "Well, why?".

"The Rebbe took this, he wrote this down... and it came to us": in context the author of the book (the Mitteler Rebbe); the block keeps "the Rebbe". In the farbrengen story "the Rebbe" is the Lubavitcher Rebbe.
The two sensitivity flags (the goyishe school, the hippies and the V-sign) are mild; flagged because they are remarks about groups.

The heart-attack story: the transcript does not show who tells it. It opens with "Right, like I was just listening" and someone answers "Yeah, I heard about that"; the teller is probably a student, and the line tying it back to the first cell ("Yeah, but you'd be able to see it with the first cell") probably Rabbi Markel's. The block frames it neutrally.
Line 40's first clause (והיינו על דרך הנזכר לעיל בידיעה שבהעלם כו') is not read in class; only the parenthetical is (alignment confidence 0.462). Its phrase is a plain rendering.
